## Descriptives

### NA

```{r}
#| label: tbl-na

# Table of valid (non-missing) cases: n (%) per wave, and persons with valid
# responses in at least 4 waves / in all waves. Only NA counts as missing
# ("DNA" is a valid category).
table_na <- function(labs, caption) {
  n_ids   <- n_distinct(df_study1$idencuesta)
  n_waves <- n_distinct(df_study1$ola)
  fmt_n   <- function(n, total) sprintf("%d (%.1f%%)", n, 100 * n / total)
  is_valid <- function(x) !is.na(x)

  # Valid cases by wave
  valid_wave <- df_study1 %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    select(ola, all_of(names(labs))) %>%
    mutate(across(-ola, is_valid)) %>%
    pivot_longer(-ola, names_to = "var", values_to = "valid") %>%
    group_by(var, ola) %>%
    summarise(txt = fmt_n(sum(valid), n()), .groups = "drop") %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = ola, values_from = txt)

  # Persons with valid responses in at least 4 waves / in all waves
  valid_person <- df_study1 %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    select(idencuesta, all_of(names(labs))) %>%
    mutate(across(-idencuesta, is_valid)) %>%
    pivot_longer(-idencuesta, names_to = "var", values_to = "valid") %>%
    group_by(var, idencuesta) %>%
    summarise(n_valid = sum(valid), .groups = "drop") %>%
    group_by(var) %>%
    summarise(`At least 4 waves` = fmt_n(sum(n_valid >= 4), n_ids),
              `All waves`        = fmt_n(sum(n_valid == n_waves), n_ids),
              .groups = "drop")

  tab <- left_join(valid_wave, valid_person, by = "var") %>%
    mutate(var = factor(var, levels = names(labs), labels = labs)) %>%
    arrange(var) %>%
    rename(Variable = var)

  kable(tab,
        format = table_format,
        align = c("l", rep("c", ncol(tab) - 1)),
        caption = caption) %>%
    kable_styling(full_width = FALSE, bootstrap_options = c("striped", "condensed")) %>%
    add_header_above(c(" " = 1, "Wave" = n_waves, "Persons" = 2))
}

na_labs <- c(ess           = "Subjective social status (own)",
             ess_og        = "Subjective social status (family of origin)",
             ess_hijos     = "Subjective social status (children)",
             merit_effort  = "Merit: effort",
             merit_talent  = "Merit: talent",
             ideo          = "Political ideology",
             sex           = "Sex",
             just_educ     = "Market justice: education",
             just_pension  = "Market justice: pensions",
             just_salud    = "Market justice: healthcare",
             educ          = "Education")

table_na(na_labs,
         "Valid cases by variable: n (%) per wave, and persons with valid responses in at least 4 waves and in all waves")
```

### Income NA

```{r}
#| label: tbl-na-income

income_labs <- c(inc_eq_real_sqrt     = "Equivalised income (CLP, Dec 2023)",
                 inc_eq_mill          = "Equivalised income (millions CLP)",
                 ln_inc_eq_real_sqrt  = "Equivalised income (log)",
                 decile_eq            = "Income decile",
                 decile_eq1           = "Income decile (DNA as category)",
                 dummy_decile10       = "Top decile (dummy)",
                 inc_group            = "Income group",
                 inc_group1           = "Income group (DNA as category)")

table_na(income_labs,
         "Valid income cases: n (%) per wave, and persons with valid income in at least 4 waves and in all waves")
```

Equivalised income, its millions-of-CLP rescaling, the decile and the top-decile dummy share the same valid cases (1,130 to 1,313 per wave; 975 persons with all six waves), with the lowest coverage in 2017. The log of income loses 35 further cases with non-positive income (950 persons with all waves). The variables that keep "DNA" as a category show full coverage because only `NA` is counted as missing; they retain 410 non-respondent cases.


### Market justice preferences

```{r}
#| label: fig-likert-just
#| fig-cap: "Distribution of market justice preferences by wave"
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 7
#| fig-align: center

just_labs <- c(just_pension = "Pensions",
               just_educ    = "Education",
               just_salud   = "Healthcare")

df_likert <- df_study1 %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(ola, all_of(names(just_labs))) %>%
  pivot_longer(-ola, names_to = "item", values_to = "resp") %>%
  filter(!is.na(resp)) %>%
  mutate(item = factor(item, levels = names(just_labs), labels = just_labs),
         resp = factor(resp, levels = levels(df_study1$just_pension))) %>%
  count(item, ola, resp) %>%
  group_by(item, ola) %>%
  mutate(prop = n / sum(n)) %>%
  ungroup()

ggplot(df_likert, aes(x = fct_rev(ola), y = prop, fill = fct_rev(resp))) +
  geom_col(width = 0.75) +
  geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(prop >= 0.05, scales::percent(prop, accuracy = 1), "")),
            position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5), size = 3, colour = "black") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = rev(met.brewer("Hiroshige", 5)),
                    breaks = levels(df_study1$just_pension),
                    guide = guide_legend(reverse = FALSE, nrow = 1)) +
  coord_flip() +
  facet_wrap(~ item, ncol = 1) +
  labs(x = "Wave", y = NULL, fill = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
        strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0))
```

### MJP index

```{r}
#| label: fig-mjp-dist
#| fig-cap: "Distribution of the market justice preferences (MJP) index by wave"
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 5.5
#| fig-align: center

df_mjp <- df_study1 %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(!is.na(mjp_index)) %>%
  mutate(mjp_bin = cut(mjp_index, breaks = seq(1, 5, by = 0.5),
                       include.lowest = TRUE, right = FALSE))

df_mjp_mean <- df_mjp %>%
  group_by(ola) %>%
  summarise(m = mean(mjp_index), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(lab = paste0("Mean = ", sprintf("%.2f", m)))

ggplot(df_mjp, aes(x = mjp_index)) +
  geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(count / tapply(count, PANEL, sum)[PANEL])),
                 breaks = seq(0.75, 5.25, by = 0.5), closed = "right",
                 fill = met.brewer("Hiroshige", 1, direction = -1)[1],
                 colour = "white") +
  geom_vline(data = df_mjp_mean, aes(xintercept = m),
             linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey20") +
  geom_text(data = df_mjp_mean, aes(x = 5, y = Inf, label = lab),
            hjust = 1, vjust = 1.5, size = 3.2, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:5) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1))) +
  facet_wrap(~ ola, nrow = 2) +
  labs(x = "MJP index (1 = strongly disagree, 5 = strongly agree)", y = NULL,
       caption = "Bins of width 0.5 centred on 1, 1.5, ..., 5. Dashed line: wave mean.") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
```

### Correlation matrix

```{r}
#| label: tbl-correlations
#| tbl-cap: "Average within-wave Spearman correlations between merit perception, subjective social status, market justice preferences, education and income"
#| tbl-cap-location: top
#| include: false

vars <- c(
  merit_effort = "Merit: Effort",
  merit_talent = "Merit: Talent",
  ess          = "Subjective social status",
  ess_og       = "Family subjective social status",
  ess_hijos    = "Son's subjective social status",
  just_pension = "Pension justice",
  just_salud   = "Healthcare justice",
  just_educ    = "Education justice",
  educyear     = "Education (years)",
  decile_eq    = "Income (decile)"
)

df_cor <- df_study1 %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(ola, all_of(names(vars))) %>%
  mutate(across(starts_with("just_"), ~ as.numeric(.x)),
         across(-ola, ~ as.numeric(.x)))

# one correlation matrix per wave
cor_waves <- df_cor %>%
  group_split(ola, .keep = FALSE) %>%
  map(~ cor(.x, method = "spearman", use = "pairwise.complete.obs"))

# average across waves on Fisher's z scale
z_mean <- Reduce(`+`, map(cor_waves, ~ atanh(pmin(pmax(.x, -0.999999), 0.999999)))) / length(cor_waves)
cor_avg <- tanh(z_mean)
diag(cor_avg) <- 1

# full matrix (with variable labels) kept for the corrplot below
cor_full <- cor_avg
rownames(cor_full) <- colnames(cor_full) <- unname(vars)

rownames(cor_avg) <- paste0(seq_along(vars), ". ", vars)
colnames(cor_avg) <- seq_along(vars)
cor_avg[upper.tri(cor_avg)] <- NA

cor_avg %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  kbl(digits = 2, format = table_format, booktabs = TRUE,
      caption = NULL) %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE) %>%
  footnote(general = paste0("Spearman correlations computed within each wave (",
                            length(cor_waves), " waves, 2016-2023) and averaged using Fisher's z."),
           general_title = "Note:", footnote_as_chunk = TRUE)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-correlations
#| fig-cap: "Average within-wave Spearman correlations (corrplot)"
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-align: center
#| include: false

corrplot(cor_full,
         method = "color",
         type = "lower",
         diag = FALSE,
         order = "original",
         addCoef.col = "black",
         number.cex = 0.75,
         number.digits = 2,
         tl.col = "black",
         tl.cex = 0.85,
         tl.srt = 45,
         cl.cex = 0.8,
         col = colorRampPalette(c("#2166AC", "white", "#B2182B"))(200),
         col.lim = c(-1, 1),
         is.corr = TRUE,
         mar = c(0, 0, 1, 0))
```


```{r}
#| label: fun-corrplot-wave
#| include: false

plot_cor_wave <- function(i) {
  m <- cor_waves[[i]]
  rownames(m) <- colnames(m) <- unname(vars)
  corrplot(m,
           method = "color",
           type = "lower",
           diag = FALSE,
           order = "original",
           addCoef.col = "black",
           number.cex = 0.75,
           number.digits = 2,
           tl.col = "black",
           tl.cex = 0.85,
           tl.srt = 45,
           cl.cex = 0.8,
           col = colorRampPalette(c("#2166AC", "white", "#B2182B"))(200),
           col.lim = c(-1, 1),
           is.corr = TRUE,
           na.label = "-",
           mar = c(0, 0, 1, 0))
}
```

### MJP ~ Mobility (MAIN EFFECTS MOBILITY)

This section describes the processing and integration into multilevel models of a series of variables created to expand the measurement of subjective social status

### SSS Index

First, we constructed an averaged index based on the three variables of subjective social status: one's own status, family of origin and one's children

```{r}
# # Subjective social status index: mean of own, family-of-origin and children's
# status (all 0-10 scales)
sss_vars <- c("ess", "ess_og", "ess_hijos")

# Internal consistency and inter-item correlations
psych::alpha(df_model[, sss_vars])$total[c("raw_alpha", "std.alpha")]
cor(df_study1[, sss_vars], use = "pairwise.complete.obs")
```

```{r}
#| label: sss-index

# Index (0-10): row mean of the three items
df_model <- df_model %>%
  mutate(sss_index = rowMeans(across(all_of(sss_vars)), na.rm = FALSE))

# Between-within decomposition
df_model <- df_model %>%
  group_by(idencuesta) %>%
  mutate(sss_index_mean = mean(sss_index),
         sss_index_cwc  = sss_index - sss_index_mean) %>%
  ungroup()
```



